body.statement:
Under ass:density-positivity, ass:density-smoothness, ass:inner-ellipticity, ass:outer-ellipticity, ass:lift-regularity, ass:fixed-separated-grid, ass:kernel-symmetry, ass:kernel-mass, ass:kernel-order, ass:four-sample-design, and ass:polynomial-bandwidth, the following estimates hold uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal F_s\).  For \(h=h_n\), every coordinate of the score \(\Psi_{g,h}\) is the sum of its frozen-coefficient, first-order-coordinate Green score and a remainder whose \(L^2(P_g)\) norm is bounded by a common constant.  In particular,
\[
 \max_{g\in\mathcal G}\lVert\Psi_{g,h_n}\rVert_{L^2(P_g)}
 \leq C\sqrt{L_n},
 \qquad
 \max_{g\in\mathcal G}\mathbb E_{P_g}\lVert\Psi_{g,h_n}(X)\rVert^4
 \leq C h_n^{-2}.
\]
For the opposite-fold adjoint scores,
\[
 \max_{g\in\mathcal G,\ r\in\{1,2\}}
 L_n^{-1/2}
 \lVert\widehat\Psi_{g,h_n}^{(-r)}-\Psi_{g,h_n}\rVert_{L^2(P_g)}
 =o_{\mathbb P}(1),
\]
and, on events whose probabilities tend to one uniformly,
\[
 \max_{g,r}\mathbb E_{P_g}
 \lVert\widehat\Psi_{g,h_n}^{(-r)}(X)\rVert^4
 \leq C h_n^{-2}.
\]
Moreover, if \(u=(u_g)_{g\in\mathcal G}\) is a zero-integral four-density perturbation, the perturbed densities are positive, and \(\max_g\lVert u_g\rVert_{C^{2,1/4}}\) is smaller than a common constant, then the selected lifted nested map in def:identified-functional obeys
\[
 \max_{1\leq j\leq J}
 \left\lVert
 \widetilde T_{P+u}(\widetilde y_j)-\widetilde T_P(\widetilde y_j)
 -\mathcal D_P[u]_j
 \right\rVert
 \leq C\left(\max_{g\in\mathcal G}
 \lVert u_g\rVert_{C^{1,1/4}}\right)^2.
\]
For the signed periodized KDEs,
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}
 \mathbb E_P\left[\max_g
 \lVert\widetilde f_g-f_g\rVert_{C^{1,1/4}}^4\right]
 \leq C\left\{
 \frac{\log n}{n h_n^{9/2}}+h_n^{2s-5/2}
 \right\}^2,
\]
and there are constants \(c_0,C_0,\epsilon_0>0\) such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}\mathbb P_P\left(
 \max_g\lVert\widetilde f_g-f_g\rVert_{C^{2,1/4}}>\epsilon_0
 \right)
 \leq C_0\exp(-c_0 n h_n^{13/2}).
\]
On the complementary good event clipping is inactive, normalization is exactly one, the selected lift branches are the population branches, all population and pilot coefficients are uniformly elliptic, and every pilot pole differs from its population pole by \(o_{\mathbb P}(h_n)\).
body.proof_tex:
Put \(\vartheta=1/4\).  All constants below depend only on
\(c,C,R,\lambda,\Lambda,\beta,\delta_0,J,K,s\) and the fixed upper
bound \(\bar\rho\), and hence not on \(P\in\mathcal F_s\).  We divide
the proof into six steps.

\emph{Step 1: uniform coefficient bounds and the local Green
parametrix.}  The change-of-variables equations for \(p\) and \(T\),
together with ass:density-positivity and the two ellipticity assumptions,
give uniform positive lower and upper eigenvalue bounds for \(A,B\), and
\(\mathsf C\).  Differentiating the two Monge--Amp\`ere equations and
using ass:density-smoothness gives, by induction, uniform
\(C^{s-2,\vartheta}\) bounds for these three matrices, for \(R_0,T\),
and for \(\alpha\).  To see that the constants are uniform, at each
induction step freeze the coefficient on a ball of fixed radius, absorb
the coefficient oscillation into the left side, apply the constant
coefficient estimate after an affine change of variables, and cover
\(\mathbb T^2\) by finitely many such balls.  For a mean-zero periodic
function, Parseval's identity gives
\[
 \lVert u\rVert_2^2=\sum_{k\neq0}|\widehat u(k)|^2
 \leq(4\pi^2)^{-1}\sum_{k\neq0}4\pi^2|k|^2|\widehat u(k)|^2
 =(4\pi^2)^{-1}\lVert\nabla u\rVert_2^2,
\]
which controls the normalization.  This proves, in particular, the
periodic Schauder estimate
\[
 \lVert v\rVert_{C^{k+2,\vartheta}}
 \leq C\lVert-\operatorname{div}(E\nabla v)\rVert_{C^{k,\vartheta}},
 \qquad \int_{\mathbb T^2}v=0,
 \tag{17}
\]
for \(E=B,\mathsf C\) and every integer \(0\leq k\leq s-4\).

Fix \(y\in\mathcal Y_J\), let \(G_B(y,z)\) be the mean-zero periodic
Green kernel of \(\mathcal L_B\), and put \(B_y=B(y)\).  The constant
coefficient fundamental solution is
\[
 \Gamma_{B_y}(z)
 =-\frac{1}{4\pi\sqrt{\det B_y}}
       \log(z^{\mathsf T}B_y^{-1}z),
 \qquad
 \nabla\Gamma_{B_y}(z)
 =-\frac{B_y^{-1}z}
 {2\pi\sqrt{\det B_y}\,z^{\mathsf T}B_y^{-1}z}.
 \tag{18}
\]
Choose a smooth cutoff equal to one in a fixed ball about zero.  Applying
\(\mathcal L_B\) to the cut-off translate of (18) leaves, away from the
Dirac mass, a divergence-form forcing whose singular part is
\[
 (B(z)-B_y)\nabla\Gamma_{B_y}(z-y),
 \qquad
 \left\lVert(B(z)-B_y)\nabla\Gamma_{B_y}(z-y)\right\rVert
 \leq C d_{\mathbb T^2}(z,y)^{-1+\vartheta}.
 \tag{19}
\]
The cutoff terms are bounded.  Solve the residual equation with zero
mean.  On a dyadic annulus of radius \(r\), rescale to a unit annulus,
apply (17) to the residual equation, and sum the geometric series
\(\sum_{m\geq0}(2^{-m}r)^{\vartheta}\).  This gives the sharper local
expansion required here,
\[
 \nabla_zG_B(y,z)=\nabla\Gamma_{B(y)}(z-y)+R_B(y,z),
 \qquad
 \lVert R_B(y,z)\rVert
 \leq C d_{\mathbb T^2}(z,y)^{-1+\vartheta}.
 \tag{20}
\]
This derivation uses the variable coefficient only through its uniform
ellipticity and \(C^{0,\vartheta}\) modulus.  Consequently its constant
is uniform over the declared class.  Notice that
\[
 \int_0^{r_0}r^{-2+2\vartheta}r\,dr<\infty.
 \tag{21}
\]
Thus the remainder in (20) is uniformly square integrable.  This is the
critical estimate not supplied by a fixed-path differentiability result.

\emph{Step 2: transformed kernels and the order-minus-two term.}
For a fixed output coordinate \(y_j\), the four leading terms in
def:nested-derivative have observation-coordinate poles
\[
 z_{C0,j}=z_{T0,j}=R_0(y_j),\qquad
 z_{C1,j}=T(y_j),\qquad z_{T1,j}=y_j.
 \tag{22}
\]
Each coordinate map in (22) is uniformly bi-Lipschitz.  In a normal
chart about its pole, write it as \(F(x)=F(z)+J_z(x-z)+E_z(x)\), where
\(\lVert E_z(x)\rVert\leq C\lVert x-z\rVert^2\).  The derivative of the
homogeneous kernel in (18) is \(O(\lVert x-z\rVert^{-2})\); hence replacing
\(F\) by its first differential changes the unsmoothed singular score by
\(O(1)\).  Convolution with the signed periodized kernel preserves this
bound in \(L^2\), because \(\lVert K_h^{\mathrm{per}}\rVert_{L^1}\) is
bounded uniformly in \(h\).  Combining this fact with (20)--(21) proves
that every exact transformed leading score differs from its frozen
coefficient, first-order-coordinate version by \(O(1)\) in
\(L^2(P_g)\), uniformly in \(g,j,P\).

For the second elliptic term of def:nested-derivative, its unsmoothed
kernel is bounded by
\[
 C\int_{\mathbb T^2}
 \frac{dz}{d_{\mathbb T^2}(y_j,z)\,d_{\mathbb T^2}(z,w)}
 \leq C\{1+|\log d_{\mathbb T^2}(y_j,w)|\}.
 \tag{23}
\]
To verify the last inequality, split the integral into the balls of
radius \(d(y_j,w)/2\) about the two poles and their complement; polar
integration handles the balls, and dyadic annuli handle the complement.
The square of the right side is integrable on \(\mathbb T^2\).  Young's
inequality therefore gives a uniform \(O(1)\) score norm after smoothing.
The coupled finite-dimensional equation determining the harmonic
translations has smooth coefficients and smooth adjoint right-hand
sides.  Estimate (17) and the branch margin in ass:lift-regularity give
a bounded score, hence bounded second and fourth moments.  This strengthens
the \(L^2\) conclusion already recorded in thm:nested-derivative without
setting either translation equal to zero.

The frozen singular score satisfies the pointwise envelope
\[
 \lVert\Psi_{g,h,j}(x)\rVert
 \leq \frac{C}{h\vee d_{\mathbb T^2}(x,z_{g,j})}
       +C\{1+|\log d_{\mathbb T^2}(x,z_{g,j})|\}.
 \tag{24}
\]
Since \(c\leq f_g\leq C\), polar integration in (24) gives
\[
 \lVert\Psi_{g,h}\rVert_2^2\leq C\log(1/h),
 \qquad
 \mathbb E\lVert\Psi_{g,h}(X)\rVert^4
 \leq C\left(h^{-4}h^2+\int_h^1r^{-4}r\,dr+1\right)
 \leq Ch^{-2}.
 \tag{25}
\]
All generated-target and harmonic terms have been retained in (23)--(25).

\emph{Step 3: the logarithmic part is unchanged by smoothing.}
Outside a ball of radius \(C_Kh\), symmetry and unit mass of the kernel
give, by Taylor expansion of (18),
\[
 K_h^{\mathrm{per}}*\nabla\Gamma_{B_y}
 =\nabla\Gamma_{B_y}+O(h^2r^{-3}).
 \tag{26}
\]
The square integral of the error in (26) is bounded because
\(h^4\int_h^{r_0}r^{-5}dr=O(1)\); the inner ball also contributes
\(O(1)\) because its area is \(O(h^2)\) and the smoothed gradient is
\(O(h^{-1})\).  Thus only the middle annulus contributes a logarithm.
With \(z=B_y^{1/2}r\omega\) and
\(\int_{\mathbb S^1}\omega\omega^{\mathsf T}d\omega=\pi I_2\), direct
integration gives
\[
 \int
 (K_h^{\mathrm{per}}*\nabla\Gamma_{B_y})(z)
 (K_h^{\mathrm{per}}*\nabla\Gamma_{B_y})(z)^{\mathsf T}dz
 =\frac{B_y^{-1}}{4\pi\sqrt{\det B_y}}\log(1/h)+O(1).
 \tag{27}
\]
If \(j\ne k\), ass:fixed-separated-grid and the uniform bi-Lipschitz
bounds keep the two poles in each observation cell a fixed distance
apart.  The product of their two \(1/r\) envelopes is integrable and is
therefore \(O(1)\).  Equations (20)--(27) prove every population score
claim in the lemma.

\emph{Step 4: KDE moments and the good event.}  For an integer
\(k\in\{0,1,2\}\), differentiation of the periodized product kernel and
a \(h\)-scale net of the torus give
\[
 \mathbb P\left(
 \lVert\widetilde f_g-\mathbb E\widetilde f_g\rVert_{C^{k,\vartheta}}>t
 \right)
 \leq Cn^C\exp(-c n h^{2+2k+2\vartheta}t^2)
 \tag{28}
\]
for \(0<t\leq1\).  Indeed, at a net point each centered summand is
bounded and has variance at most \(Ch^{-2-2k-2\vartheta}\).  The elementary
exponential-moment calculation
\[
 \mathbb P\left(\left|n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nZ_i\right|>t\right)
 \leq2\exp\left\{-\frac{nt^2}{2(\sigma^2+Mt/3)}\right\}
\]
when \(|Z_i|\leq M\) and \(n^{-1}\sum_i\mathbb E Z_i^2\leq\sigma^2\)
follows by expanding \(\mathbb E e^{aZ_i}\), bounding the terms of order
three and higher by the geometric series in \(aM\), and optimizing over
\(a\).  Apply this bound at the net points; the next derivative controls
interpolation between them, and a union bound produces only the displayed
polynomial factor.  Taylor's formula, the vanishing
moments through order \(s-1\), and periodicity give
\[
 \lVert\mathbb E\widetilde f_g-f_g\rVert_{C^{k,\vartheta}}
 \leq Ch^{s-k-\vartheta}.
 \tag{29}
\]
Integrating the tail in (28), adding (29), and using the four-cell union
bound yields
\[
 \mathbb E\max_g\lVert\widetilde f_g-f_g\rVert_{C^{1,\vartheta}}^4
 \leq C\left\{\frac{\log n}{nh^{9/2}}+h^{2s-5/2}\right\}^2.
 \tag{30}
\]
Taking \(k=2\), a fixed sufficiently small \(\epsilon_0\), and then
using (29) gives
\[
 \mathbb P\left(\max_g
 \lVert\widetilde f_g-f_g\rVert_{C^{2,\vartheta}}>\epsilon_0\right)
 \leq C_0e^{-c_0nh^{13/2}}.
 \tag{31}
\]
On this event's complement, \(\widetilde f_g\geq c/2\).  Since the
periodized kernel has mass one, \(\int\widetilde f_g=1\), so clipping is
inactive, the normalizing denominator is one, and
\(\widehat f_g=\widetilde f_g\).  The unconditional Hölder moment in
(30) is deliberately stated for the smooth signed pilot: the clipped
maximum need not be differentiable on the exceptional event.  Equality
on the good event and the bounded fallback are exactly what the map and
risk arguments require.

\emph{Step 5: tame quadratic expansion and pole rate.}  The fixed-path
differentiability substrate is recorded in
lem:fixed-path-ma-linearization-source.  We now derive the stronger
uniform quadratic estimate needed for shrinking-bandwidth directions.
For two by two
matrices the exact identity
\[
 \det(M+E)=\det M+\operatorname{cof}(M):E+\det E
 \tag{32}
\]
shows that the remainder in each Monge--Amp\`ere determinant is quadratic
in the Hessian increment.  The product and composition inequalities
\[
 \lVert uv\rVert_{C^{1,\vartheta}}
 \leq C\lVert u\rVert_{C^{1,\vartheta}}
        \lVert v\rVert_{C^{1,\vartheta}},
 \quad
 \lVert u\circ(F+v)-u\circ F-Du\circ F\,v\rVert_{C^{0,\vartheta}}
 \leq C\lVert u\rVert_{C^{2,\vartheta}}
        \lVert v\rVert_{C^{1,\vartheta}}^2
 \tag{33}
\]
follow from the fundamental theorem of calculus.  Apply (32)--(33) first
to the inner equation, next to the exact generated-density identity
\[
 q(z)=f_{C1}(z)(f_{T0}/f_{C0})(p^{-1}(z)),
 \tag{34}
\]
and finally to the outer equation.  Division in (34) is legitimate
because every density on the good event is at least \(c/2\).  Estimate
(17) absorbs the three linearized equations.  The small
\(C^{2,\vartheta}\) norm keeps every interpolating coefficient uniformly
elliptic.  This yields
\[
 \max_j\left\lVert
 \widetilde T_{P+u}(\widetilde y_j)-\widetilde T_P(\widetilde y_j)
 -\mathcal D_P[u]_j\right\rVert
 \leq C\left(\max_g\lVert u_g\rVert_{C^{1,\vartheta}}\right)^2.
 \tag{35}
\]
The selected translation is the cell average of the lifted displacement.
The margin \(\Delta_{\mathrm{lift}}(P)>\beta\) prevents a branch change
under the same small perturbation; integrating the map expansion proves
that its translation remainder also satisfies (35).  Thus (35) includes,
rather than deletes, the translation-aware branch derivative.

Applying the corresponding first-order Schauder stability estimate in
\(C^{0,\vartheta}\) to the two transports and (34) gives
\[
 \lVert\widehat p-p\rVert_{C^1}
 +\lVert\widehat T-T\rVert_{C^1}
 +\lVert\widehat B-B\rVert_{C^{0,\vartheta}}
 =O_{\mathbb P}\left(
 \sqrt{\frac{\log n}{nh^{5/2}}}+h^{s-1/4}\right).
 \tag{36}
\]
Every pole in (22) is a composition of these maps, so its distance from
the pilot pole is bounded by the right side of (36).  After division by
\(h\), this becomes
\[
 O_{\mathbb P}\left(
 \sqrt{\frac{\log n}{nh^{9/2}}}+h^{s-5/4}
 \right)=o_{\mathbb P}(1)
 \tag{37}
\]
by lem:bandwidth-feasibility.  This proves the asserted
\(o_{\mathbb P}(h_n)\) moving-pole rate.

\emph{Step 6: estimated singular scores.}  The resolvent identity
\[
 \mathcal L_{\widehat B}^{-1}-\mathcal L_B^{-1}
 =\mathcal L_{\widehat B}^{-1}
 \operatorname{div}\{(\widehat B-B)\nabla\mathcal L_B^{-1}\}
 \tag{38}
\]
and the same dyadic calculation as in Step 1 show that changing a
coefficient or a \(C^1\) coordinate map changes a smoothed pole score by
at most its perturbation size times \(C\sqrt{\log(1/h)}\), up to a bounded
remainder.  A pole translation by distance \(d\) costs at most \(Cd/h\)
in \(L^2\), since the derivative of the smoothed \(1/r\) kernel has
\(L^2\) norm \(O(h^{-1})\).  Consequently,
\[
 \lVert\widehat U_h-U_h\rVert_2
 \leq C\left\{
 (\lVert\widehat B-B\rVert_{C^{0,\vartheta}}
  +\lVert\widehat F-F\rVert_{C^1})\sqrt{\log(1/h)}
 +\frac{d(\widehat z,z)}h+1\right\}.
 \tag{39}
\]
Equations (36)--(37) make (39) \(o_{\mathbb P}(\sqrt{L_n})\).  The
order-minus-two and harmonic terms remain bounded by Steps 1--2.  The
pointwise envelope (24) continues to hold on the pilot event, so the
fourth-moment calculation (25) applies conditionally.  Cross-fitting
makes each opposite-fold pilot independent of the corresponding
evaluation fold.  This proves the two adjoint-score assertions and
completes the lemma.
